summary.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

setting_and_object.category: Architecture / reasoning system (built on the BDH post-Transformer family)

details: Chain-of-thought reasoning couples computation to serially generated language tokens, inflating token use, latency and inference cost, while existing compact recursive latent solvers (HRM/TRM) need per-task optimization and task identity embeddings rather than learning an unseen transformation purely from demonstrations at inference time.

BDH-CQ: a system that unifies in-context learning with recurrent latent reasoning — demonstrations are ingested sequentially to update a fixed-parameter recurrent associative memory S_t (no growing KV cache, no weight updates or task IDs at inference), and the query is then answered by iterating a shared update on a high-dimensional structured latent workspace H_r conditioned on S_K, decoding only the final answer.
Intermediate reasoning is never verbalized; test-time compute is scaled by the number of latent iterations ('reasoning effort'). Exact dimensions, update rules and training recipe are proprietary.
Single 150M-parameter configuration; trained to predict exact ARC output grids after preceding demonstration pairs are absorbed into recurrent context.
Mixture of privately curated ARC-style data plus public ARC-AGI-1 training set, RE-ARC, ConceptARC, ARC-Heavy, ARC-GEN100K, with additional augmentation.
No evaluation-task demonstrations or task identifiers used in training; training also varies latent reasoning effort so effort can be chosen at inference.
400-task public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation split, leaderboard two-attempt pass@2 convention (pass@1 and test-pair accuracy also reported).
Cost computed from measured hardware time: ~0.85 H200 GPU-seconds/task at $3/H200-hour = $0.00070/task; compared against ARC Prize leaderboard reported costs (GPT 5.6 Luna Low, HRM $1.48, TRM $1.76).
Independent black-box audit by co-authors from Bielik AI and NYU, without weight access, plus ConceptARC and a hand-crafted set.
ConceptARC: 160 tasks / 16 concept families, strict task accuracy (all 3 test inputs correct) vs test-pair accuracy; replicated with cryptographically opaque task IDs and concept-mixed batches.

Four complexity ladders with 3 demonstrations and held-out inputs beyond demonstrated ranges: boundary propagation distance, number of motif copies, sorting sequence length, nesting depth; plus a 'matched support' variant adding one demonstration at test complexity on byte-identical inputs.

Contextual binding: fresh per-task color permutations with 2–8 simultaneous bindings; composition: reflection / color swap / rotation alone vs composed with relocation, across one fixed-layout and two shuffled 3x3 motif families (72 outputs per condition).

Appendix cohorts: calibrated generated 400-task set, 1,131-task mechanic-stratified generated set (GPT-5.6 authored), and ten deterministic 12x12 'ladders' (40 tasks per condition) for conditional rule selection, unseen parameters, panel count/separation, support chains.
Reasoning effort tiers LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH; MIN vs STANDARD effort on the full public set with paired McNemar test.
Repeatability check via repeated identical requests; permutation nulls and Wilson intervals for descriptive statistics.

key_findings.finding: A 150M-parameter latent-reasoning system attains competitive ARC-AGI-1 accuracy at radically lower cost, breaking the reported cost–accuracy Pareto frontier.
key_findings.evidence: 29.5% pass@2 (24.25% pass@1; 118/400 tasks) at a computed $0.00070 per task (~0.85 H200 GPU-s); roughly 57x cheaper than GPT 5.6 Luna (Low) at 34.2%/$0.040 per leaderboard data (~11x after OpenAI's 80% price cut), versus $1.48 (HRM) and $1.76 (TRM); score reproduced by an independent black-box audit.

key_findings.finding: Whether a demonstrated operation extrapolates depends largely on demonstration coverage, and coverage failures are distinguishable from execution bottlenecks.
key_findings.evidence: Propagation (distances 2–8) and copying (1–4 sites) are 48/48 correct, while ordering falls from near-saturation to 29/36 at length 6, 8/24 at 7, 1/24 at 8, and nesting falls to 29/36 at depth 5. With byte-identical inputs, adding one demonstration at test complexity raises depth-5 nesting from 19/24 to 24/24 and length-8 ordering from 0/24 to 13/24; at length 8 only 3/24 outputs even had correct dimensions, whereas all depth-5 nesting outputs had correct dimensions with >99.9% cell accuracy.

key_findings.finding: The recurrent memory binds dense novel task-specific mappings reliably, but composing operations with relocation is representation-dependent rather than uniformly hard.
key_findings.evidence: Fresh per-task color permutations are applied correctly on 96/96 held-out outputs at rank one (24/24 at 2, 4, 6, 8 simultaneous bindings). Rotation+relocation 72/72, reflection+relocation 47/72, color swap 26/72 alone (only in the fixed-layout family; 1/24 in each shuffled family) and 0/72 composed.

key_findings.finding: Successful outputs often do not reflect a consistently applied rule within a task, and this is not explained by request-side cues.
key_findings.evidence: On ConceptARC, pass@2 test-pair accuracy is 77.92% vs 59.38% strict task accuracy; 52/160 tasks have one or two correct test inputs but fail as tasks. Replacing semantic task IDs with opaque labels and mixing concept batches leaves aggregates unchanged (374/480 pairs in both; 96 vs 95 tasks; 6 semantic-only and 6 opaque-only successes), though only 276/480 full candidate lists agreed.

key_findings.finding: Accuracy scales monotonically with latent reasoning effort, and diagnostic ladders localize sharp limits in conditionally selecting/parameterizing demonstrated rules and in multi-panel segmentation.
key_findings.evidence: Pass@2 is 21% (LOW), 27% (MEDIUM), 29.5% (HIGH) with 22%/11%/0% cost reduction; MIN effort costs one third of STANDARD ($0.00088 vs $0.00265) for 111/400 vs 118/400 (McNemar p=0.167). In controlled ladders, genuine two-rule selection by a marker drops to 56.7% versus 40/40 on a matched varying-marker control; a shift parameter absent from demonstrations gives 0/120 versus 12/40 when demonstrated; panel union drops from 26/40 (two separated panels) to 1/40 (three panels) and 3/40 (touching panels); support chains decline 80%→27.5% from one to eight dependent objects while three independent objects remain 40/40.
